title: Autocompletion: Don't call const functions
body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109193
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57669

Supersedes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/85361

Makes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109211 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109218 not required anymore CC @clayjohn 

Autocompletion does not only rely on Godot analyzer types, but does some additional inference work beforehand. One of the approaches for this, was to actually call some functions and deduce a type from the returned value.

This however disregards that calling those functions might have side effects, e.g. in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109193 the called function would allocate memory. The `const` identifier is not a strict enough check to assume that there are no side effects.

This PR removes this behavior completely. This might break some cases that currently work, but the actual impact is limited:

Due to a bug in the original code, only `const` methods which can be called without providing arguments would actually be executed (notice how no values ever get added to `args` in the old code). So I read through all `const` methods which can take no args to evaluate the actual impact. The methods can be split into certain groups:

- Having an annotated builtin return type that is not a container type and not `Variant` -> the return value provides the same results as the type hint, no impact
- The method is declared on some ref counted class which there is no way to obtain a constant instance of -> e.g. `PhysicsTestMotionResult2D` -> would never be called due to no constant base object
- The method is a property getter -> no one actually uses property getters in GDScript, they are not even suggested by autocompletion. Using the property is a completely different code path anyway
- The method accesses some dynamic object state -> e.g. get_currently_focused_control -> using the static type hint is safer anyway since the state while editing might not match the runtime state
- Same for a lot of methods that return object types that can be polymorphic -> calling it would yield the correct polymorphic type but I'd argue that just leads to unsafe suggestions, users should use casting and type checking if the code relies on receiving a certain subtype

The main use case for this piece of code are methods which return a structured dictionary. For those autocompletion can actually suggest the keys. I added dummy results for the limited set of methods to which this applied.

I also added some special handling for `duplicate` methods since those can be quite handy IMO. Other than that most effected results are either too unsafe or so unlikely to actually hit, that we can add a special case if anyone actually notices the change.

> This PR also removes some code that is duplicated with the analyzer. GDScript utility functions and Builtin type constructors are always correctly resolved by the analyzer we don't need special code in the completion for it. I also removed the `get_node` special case. It was dead code due to the `args` bug mentioned above.
